reason: E1 supports the claim that coherent nanoprecipitates improve strength-ductility synergy by facilitating dislocation transmission and relieving stress, but it provides no evidence on radiation tolerance, helium sink behaviour, or post-irradiation ductility retention. E2 shows in-situ TiC formation in a W-based HEA and mentions the need for irradiation studies, but does not test or support the radiation-tolerance mechanism. Thus, the structural and processing premises are partly supported, while the radiation-specific premises lack direct cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preventing premature crack initiation
Coherent nanoprecipitates can be introduced in a stepwise controllable manner in W-based refractory HEAs
In-situ TiC or similar phases can be formed in W-based HEAs via powder metallurgy processing
Nanoprecipitate sites act as sinks for helium and irradiation-induced defects, reducing bubble formation and hardening
The nanoprecipitate-enhanced alloy will retain tensile ductility after irradiation compared to the unmodified alloy
